name: pest
description: PEG parser generator with external .pest grammar files and a generic Pair tree; large user base

approach.comment: Per Assessment Guidelines: PEG grammar in a `.pest` file, parser generated by `#[derive(Parser)] #[grammar = "..."]` (pest_derive).

implementation.comment: Runtime deps are ucd-trie and memchr (plus optional serde/serde_json/miette); no C/C++ in the tree.

crates-io.comment: `pest` is the runtime crate; `pest_derive` (proc-macro), `pest_generator`, and `pest_meta` are siblings released in lockstep.

documentation.comment: The pest book is the primary guide; API reference at docs.rs/pest.

grammar-class.comment: Parsing expression grammar with ordered choice, lookahead predicates, and a grammar-level stack (PUSH/POP/PEEK) for context-sensitive tricks.

grammar-definition.comment: `.pest` file referenced via `#[grammar = "path"]`; `#[grammar_inline = "..."]` also allows an inline string.

left-recursion.comment: PEG: left-recursive rules loop forever and must be rewritten. `pest::pratt_parser::PrattParser` handles operator precedence/associativity over the resulting flat token sequence (deprecated `prec_climber` still present).

ambiguity-handling.comment: `|` tries alternatives in order and commits to the first match; failed alternatives never consume input.

backtracking.comment: Full backtracking on failed alternatives via checkpoint/restore; no cut/commit operator in the grammar.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless: grammar operates directly on characters; atomic (`@`/`$`) rules play the token role. No token-stream input.

unicode-aware.comment: Positions advance by `char` with UTF-8 boundary validation; grammar supports `'\u{..}'` ranges, `ANY`, and Unicode category builtins (via ucd-trie).

streaming-partial-input.comment: Requires the complete input `&str`; no incomplete/need-more signal.

zero-copy.comment: `Pair<'i, R>` borrows `&'i str`; `as_str()`/`as_span()` slice the input without copying.

span-tracking.comment: `Span::start()/end()` byte offsets on every pair; `Position::line_col()`/`Pair::line_col()` computed on demand.

output-model.comment: Untyped `Pairs`/`Pair` tree keyed by the generated `Rule` enum; users convert to their own AST afterwards (helper crates pest-ast/from-pest exist).

semantic-actions.comment: No actions in the grammar; walk `Pairs` after parsing (or feed them to `PrattParser`).

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: Optional `WHITESPACE`/`COMMENT` rules are inserted implicitly in sequences and repetitions, disabled inside atomic rules.

stateful-parsing.comment: No user-defined state threaded through the parse. Only the grammar-level string stack (PUSH/POP/PEEK) is available, which covers indentation/here-doc cases but not symbol tables.

error-recovery.comment: Parse stops at the first failure; the checkpoint/restore mechanism is for backtracking, not recovery. No skip/sync API.

expected-token-reporting.comment: `ErrorVariant::ParsingError { positives, negatives }` lists expected/unexpected rules at the farthest position; `set_error_detail(true)` adds call-stack attempt info.

custom-error-types.comment: Error type is fixed to `pest::error::Error<R>`; users can only construct `ErrorVariant::CustomError { message }` (e.g. in post-walk validation), not substitute their own type.

error-span-fidelity.comment: `Error.location` is `InputLocation::Pos(usize)` or `Span((usize, usize))` plus `line_col`; renders a pointer/underline. No labelled secondary spans on the native type (miette adapter adds a single labelled span).

contextual-error-messages.comment: `Error::renamed_rules(|rule| ...)` maps rule names to human-readable labels; `Error::new_from_span` + `CustomError` for hand-written messages. No per-sub-expression labels inside the grammar itself.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Implicit WHITESPACE/COMMENT matches are silent and produce no tokens; spans still cover the original text but trivia is not represented as nodes.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: No verified use by rust-analyzer, Helix, Zed, or Neovim. (Prisma's language tooling uses pest for its schema parser, but that is not one of the listed editors.)

runtime-speed-tier.comment: parse-rosetta-rs JSON benchmark (rustc 1.94.1, checked 2026-09-19): pest v2.8.6 62 ms vs hand-written serde_json 18 ms (~3.4x), slower than winnow (27), peg (29), lalrpop (40), chumsky (47), combine (53); slightly faster than nom 8 (68).

compile-time-impact.comment: parse-rosetta-rs full build: 3 s for pest (winnow 1 s, lalrpop 12 s). Proc-macro pipeline (pest_derive -> pest_generator -> syn) plus one closure-heavy function per rule; generated code scales linearly with grammar size.

allocation-strategy.comment: Tokens are appended to a single flat `Rc<Vec<QueueableToken>>` queue (arena-like); `Pair`s are cheap views into it. Not allocation-free (requires `alloc`), no per-node boxing.

generated-code-size.comment: No parse tables; one recursive-descent function per rule. parse-rosetta-rs binary overhead 119 KiB (lalrpop 1,523 KiB, grmtools 2,612 KiB).

no-std-support.comment: `#![no_std]` with `alloc` required; build with `--no-default-features`. CI has a dedicated `no_std` job (`-Z build-std=core,alloc --no-default-features`).

unsafe-usage.comment: No `unsafe` blocks found in position.rs, span.rs, parser_state.rs, error.rs, or iterators/pair.rs (only safe `core::ptr::eq`), but the crate does not declare `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, so tagged minimal rather than forbid.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: Normal usage requires `pest_derive` (`proc-macro = true`). Implementing `Parser` by hand via `pest::state` is technically possible but not the supported workflow.

build-rs-step.comment: Grammar compiled by the derive macro at compile time; no build script. Note: editing only the `.pest` file may not trigger a rebuild due to proc-macro caching.

dependency-count.comment: Runtime crate `pest` with default features: ucd-trie, memchr. Optional: serde, serde_json (`pretty-print`), miette (`miette-error`). Build-time `pest_derive` pulls pest_generator/pest_meta/syn/quote/proc-macro2.

wasm-compatible.comment: Pure Rust, `no_std`-capable, no platform-specific deps; the pest.rs site runs pest compiled to WASM (per issue #430). Grammar must be embedded at compile time (`grammar`/`grammar_inline`), not loaded from disk at runtime.

async-friendly.comment: `Pairs`/`Pair` hold an `Rc<Vec<..>>` and are therefore not `Send`; input must be a complete `&str`. `Error<R>` is Send + Sync.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads of `pest`, checked 2026-09-19 (~23.4M/month per lib.rs).

maintenance-status.comment: Three releases in the last 3 months (2.8.8 Jul, 2.9.0 Aug, 2.9.1 Sep 2026); last push 2026-09-18; repo not archived.

documentation-quality.comment: pest book (grammar syntax, calculator/CSV/JSON examples, PrattParser) plus 100%-documented API reference. No formal migration guides between minor versions, so not 5.

notable-users.value: handlebars-rust (template engine), Prisma engines (schema-ast PSL parser), ZoKrates (zk DSL parser)
notable-users.comment: All verified via Cargo.toml. Tera 2.x no longer depends on pest (checked tera/Cargo.toml).

bus-factor.comment: pest-parser GitHub org; crate owners tomtau, dragostis, and the org team. Original author dragostis dominates history (623 commits); tomtau is the current primary maintainer, with a handful of recurring contributors.
